resources.string: Shows a short pause before the apps you picked.

BlueApp only uses this to know which app just opened, so it can show a pause before the apps you chose. It does not read what is on your screen, does not see what you type, and has no internet access, so nothing ever leaves your phone.
Your thumb knows where TikTok is before you\'ve decided to open it. BlueApp puts a short pause in the way so you get to decide.

⏸ A pause every time you open a chosen app: a countdown or a quick challenge.

🎲 It's different every time, so it can't become a habit you tap through.

⏱ You choose how long you need. When time's up, the app closes.

🔋 Event driven, no background polling. Nothing leaves your phone.
Tap to add or remove. Changes apply right away.
TikTok, Instagram and YouTube are recommended and already selected. Add any other app you open without thinking.
We recommend TikTok, Instagram and YouTube, but none are installed. Pick the apps you open without thinking.
How long can one session last?
After each pause you choose how long you need, up to this limit. When it runs out, the app closes and the next round needs a new pause.
BlueApp needs to know when a chosen app opens. That\'s all it looks at.
Used only to detect which app just came to the front. BlueApp can\'t read your screen or what you type, and it has no internet permission. In the list, open BlueApp → turn on “BlueApp pause”.
Switch greyed out? Android blocks this for apps installed outside the Play Store. Tap App info → ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings, then try again.
Optional. Some phones (Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo, Huawei…) won\'t let the pause screen open without it.
Pauses stay off until Accessibility is enabled. You can turn it on from the home screen.
Opening a guarded app will show a pause first.
Enable “BlueApp pause” in Accessibility settings so the pause can appear.
On, but no apps are selected yet.
Longest single session after a pause, in minutes.
Battery: BlueApp has no background service, timers or network. Android only wakes it when an app comes to the front, and the session timer exists only while a session is running.
Let go early and it starts over.
Count them, then type the number.
%1$d digits. They disappear in a moment.
You spent %1$d min on %2$s. Good moment to stop?
Applies everywhere, including the pause screen.
Primary and secondary colours from your wallpaper. Follows dark mode.
True black for OLED screens. Easiest on the battery.
